title: House Republicans send Massie's Hegseth impeachment articles to committee, 211 to 204
dek: A Republican congressman forced a House vote on removing the Pentagon's chief. It ended on Tuesday with the articles sent to committee, which blocks a floor vote in this Congress.
what: On Monday, 9 November 2026, Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, read articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor. CBS News and CNN report the resolution runs 34 pages and has eight articles.

CBS reports that three articles say Hegseth waged war on Iran without congressional authorization. Others cover civilian casualties, boat strikes in the Caribbean, the capture of Venezuela's president, and Pentagon scrutiny of Sen. Mark Kelly over a video urging service members to refuse illegal orders. These are Massie's allegations.

CBS reports that Massie first introduced similar articles in September, and House Republican leaders put off action until November. It reports that because the resolution is privileged, leaders must schedule a vote within two legislative days. CNN's live coverage says a vote is expected on Wednesday.

CBS quotes Hegseth calling it political theater: "Didn't work against President Trump, and it won't work with me." It reports that Rep. James Comer pointed to voter frustration over Iran policy and Rep. Don Bacon said he is "wrestling" with it, while Democrats largely support the effort. A local station report says Massie lost his primary and will not return to Congress next term. I did not confirm that elsewhere.

On Tuesday, 10 November 2026, the House voted 211 to 204 on a motion to refer the resolution to the Judiciary Committee, according to CBS News and Time. CBS reports the motion effectively kills it. All 203 Democrats voting and Massie, the only Republican to do so, voted against the motion. 211 Republicans voted for it.

CBS reports that 11 Democrats and 7 Republicans did not vote. Posts on X name the 11 Democrats and say that seven more no votes would have defeated the motion. I did not check that count or any claim in those posts about why they were absent.

CBS quotes Massie afterward: "I wasn't surprised, but I was disappointed." Time reports that Democrats, who take control of the House on 3 January 2027, could bring impeachment articles to the floor again.
why: It is rare for a member of the president's own party to force an impeachment vote on a cabinet officer. The outcome turned on a procedural motion and on who was absent, which is why posts about the absences spread.
next: Whether Democrats bring articles against Hegseth to the floor after they take control of the House on 3 January 2027.

corrections.text: The story said a vote was expected on Wednesday. The House voted on Tuesday, 10 November, and sent the articles to committee. Title, summary and status updated.
